Tanya (Customer): Hey team — during a deploy this morning we had a ~90s spike and started getting tons of 429s. App is on the standard hosted plan (org_id: org_123). Spike window ~2026-03-12T09:12Z -> 2026-03-12T09:14Z. We saw requests fail with `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and clients reported `Retry-After` sometimes missing. Example log snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2026 09:12:43 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 0
X-Request-Id: req_abc123
```
Can you explain how burst credits / smoothing work and whether we should be parked on a dedicated pool for this workload?

Emily (Support): Sorry you're running into this, Tanya — I pulled a quick trace for org_123 for that window. A couple quick Qs while we dig: 1) do you have client-side rate limiting/pacing? 2) are you sending many concurrent streams (streaming responses) or short high-RPS requests? Also sharing our burst policy in a sec.

Tanya (Customer): No client-side smoothing right now, we rely on retries from the SDK. Mostly lots of small requests (chat completions) at high concurrency — burst came from a traffic redirect during a deploy.

Raj (Infra): Pinging with the infra view. We hit the burst credit pool for org_123. Short summary of how our hosted burst model works (simplified): baseline rate is your plan limit (e.g., 100 rps). We allow transient bursts up to ~3x baseline for short windows by consuming "burst credits". Credits are a token bucket that refill slowly; in our current config refill ~= 1 credit per second (per baseline unit) and capacity ~= baseline * 60s. Practically that means you can spike for tens of seconds; sustained higher-than-baseline traffic will exhaust credits and then you'll get 429s until credits refill.

Raj (Infra): For your specific spike: baseline ~100 rps, spike peaked ~800 rps for ~45s -> that consumed credits and hit throttling. We also saw ~30% of 429 responses missing `Retry-After` because the throttling happened inside the router layer while we propagated headers — we're fixing that next deploy.

Tanya (Customer): Got it. Is there a way to request a temporary burst top-up for a big planned launch? Also curious about smoothing guidance we can implement quickly.

Kevin (Platform): We can do two things short-term: 1) emergency top-up of burst credits for org_123 (requires billing approval) — we can add a one-off 60s-300s credit boost; 2) recommend client-side smoothing to avoid synchronized retries sweeping through. For longer-term, Dedicated or Reserved capacity is the right fit for predictable high spikes. @Emily can confirm billing flow.

Emily (Support): To request top-up, open a ticket with billing approval or share the billing contact here; ops will apply a temporary credit allocation. Meanwhile, quick smoothing recipes:
- implement a token-bucket limiter on the client with capacity = baseline * 2 and refill = baseline (per second), drop or queue excess
- use exponential backoff + full jitter on 429s and honor `Retry-After` header
- if you have queued bursty work, spread it across a ~60s window (leaky-bucket)

Emily (Support): Example client pseudo-config (JS):
```js
// simple token bucket
const capacity = 200; // baseline 100 * 2
let tokens = capacity;
const refillPerSec = 100; // baseline
setInterval(() => { tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + refillPerSec); }, 1000);
async function send(req) {
  if (tokens <= 0) { await sleep(50); return send(req); } // simple delay
  tokens -= 1;
  return fetch(req);
}
```

rate-limiter-bot: System notice: org_123 consumed 100% of burst credits at 2026-03-12T09:12:44Z; throttles applied.

ops-bot: Auto-scaling event: routed 12% of traffic to fallback model variant `gptx-compact` while autoscaler attempted to add capacity.

Tanya (Customer): That JS snippet helps. Any recommended retry/backoff params?

Raj (Infra): We suggest initial retry delay 300ms, max backoff 5s, full jitter. Also, prefer retrying idempotent calls only; for chat-like streams, consider coalescing or batching multiple prompts into a single request when possible.

Kevin (Platform): Regarding `Retry-After` header — our stack will be patched so throttles consistently return `Retry-After` in next deploy. For now, if you see missing header, treat 429 as ~1s +/- jitter.

Emily (Support): Next steps for us: 1) Emily to coordinate a one-off burst credit top-up if billing approves; 2) Raj to open an infra follow-up to ensure `Retry-After` propagation and make burst-credit metrics visible in Console; 3) Tanya team to roll out token-bucket smoothing + jittered backoff.

Tanya (Customer): I'll get billing approval and start the smoothing changes this afternoon. Can we ask for a 3-minute temporary top-up to cover the planned launch?

Kevin (Platform): That sounds reasonable — Emily, please share the billing contact DM and we'll queue the top-up. :thumbsup:

Emily (Support): Copying checklist in-thread: 
- collect billing consent (Tanya)
- add temporary +180s burst credits (Platform)
- infra follow-up: ensure `Retry-After` on all throttles (Raj)
- monitoring: add alert if burst-credit-remaining < 20% during window (Emily)

Tanya (Customer): Thanks all, will DM billing and post back here once done. Appreciate the fast responses.

Emily (Support): Happy to help — keep this thread updated and we'll close once you confirm top-up applied and smoothing rolled out. :white_check_mark:
